answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
While the scientific integrity of the “physical matching” method for Scope 2 is not defensible, marginal impact accounting is.

Similar to the way financial impact is measured in dollars using a marginal price multiplied by the volume of energy consumed or produced, carbon impact can similarly be measured in tons of carbon using marginal emissions rates multiplied by the volume of energy consumed or produced.

This concept is neither new nor novel [1].

[1] Rudkevich, A. M. & Ruiz, P. A. (2012). Locational Carbon Footprint of the Power Industry:
Implications for Operations, Planning and Policy Making. In Zheng, Q. P., Rebennack, S., Pardalos, P. M., Pereira, M. V. F. & Iliadis, N. A. (Eds.), Handbook of CO₂ in Power
Systems (pp. 131–165-131–165). http://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-64227431-2_8.
